doc.title: Don Menza and Sam Noto interviewed by Monk Rowe, Clinton, New York, January 28, 1997

title: Noto on arranging and writing for Bellson
summary: Noto studied arranging with Wes Hensel in Vegas, and Louie Bellson played his chart 'A Couple of Dozen'.

story.theme_name: Writing and arranging: how musicians compose
story.community_name: Writing, arranging and composing: how the music gets made

blocks.x: While we’re talking about great arrangers, you guys have written a great deal of music yourself, and was it a self-taught thing, or did you — from listening again and trying things out?

Well he’s into the writing now maybe more than I am. I was in Vegas in house bands, and I got a little bored with that so I started studying with one of the trumpet players, Wes Hensel, who was on the band, as far as arranging you know. And he gave me pointers and that, so I wrote some charts. But Don is really into the writing, and I don’t write as much as I should really, anymore.
You wrote some things for Rob McConnell, didn’t you?

No, I played on a couple. No I’ve never written. I’ve written a bunch of things that I’ve played in Buffalo with a local band, you know, we put a concert on. But I’ve never — Louie Bellson played one of my charts in his big band, called “A Couple of Dozen,” which is based on a row you know.
Not a Monk Rowe. You don’t want to base a tune on me. That was good.

I forgot.. I made a pun and I didn’t know it. MR. Well, Don, I think that there’s probably a significant number of saxophone players in this country who have a kind of a love-hate relationship with you.
